title: MCP route with bearer-token auth exposing get_balances
outcome: An MCP route (e.g. app/mcp/route.ts) exposes exactly one tool, get_balances, backed by m2-001's shared SimpleFin module, and is protected by a static bearer-token check read from a server-side-only env var. This is a security-sensitive task: the bearer key comparison must be timing-safe, and the SimpleFin access URL must never appear in any response.
acceptance: The MCP route is implemented using the Model Context Protocol SDK (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk) and a Next.js-compatible adapter (e.g. mcp-handler, matching js/ember-finance's dependency choice) rather than a hand-rolled JSON-RPC parser -- reuse the proven pattern rather than reinventing MCP framing.
Exactly one tool is registered: get_balances, taking no required arguments, returning the same grouped-by-institution data as m2-001's shared module / the dashboard page.

A bearer token is read from an Authorization: Bearer header or a ?key= query param, compared against MCP_BEARER_KEY (a new server-side-only env var) using crypto.timingSafeEqual (not ===, which is not timing-safe) or an equivalent constant-time comparison.

A missing or incorrect bearer key is rejected before get_balances is invoked (no SimpleFin call is attempted). The rejection response must not be a bare 401 with no body if that would trigger an MCP client's OAuth auto-registration attempt. If ../ember-finance/src/app/api/mcp/route.ts is readable from this task's working directory, read it first and follow its exact response shape for this failure mode (it solved this same problem already) rather than guessing; if it is not accessible, research the MCP spec's expected error shape for this case and note the assumption in the completion report.

MCP_BEARER_KEY is added to .env.example with a one-line comment marking it a credential that must never be committed; if unset, the route fails closed (rejects all requests) rather than allowing unauthenticated access.

No response from the route -- success or error, authenticated or rejected -- ever contains the SimpleFin access URL, its embedded credential, or SimpleFin's raw auth headers. Verify this with an automated test, not just inspection.

Tests cover: correct-key success returning demo-bridge data, missing-key rejection, wrong-key rejection, and the credential-never-leaks assertion above. Tests must use SimpleFin's public demo bridge or a mock -- never a real access URL.
The repository's required verification command (./scripts/verify-task.sh) passes.
